questions.q: Choose the correct article: “____ Ganga is a holy river.”
questions.why: Names of rivers take 'the'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Find the error: “The results of the survey was surprising.”
questions.why: The subject is 'results' (plural): 'were'. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “The cook prepares the meal every day.”
opts: The meal was prepared by the cook every day.
The meal is prepared by the cook every day.
The meal is preparing by the cook every day.
The meal prepared by the cook every day.
questions.why: Present simple passive: is/are + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. First, she boiled water.
Q. Finally, she served the tea hot.
R. Next, she added tea leaves and milk.
S. Then she poured it into cups.
questions.why: Order follows the cues: First, Next, Then, Finally. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the one word for: “A cure for all diseases”
questions.why: Panacea means a cure-all. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct version: “I am living in Panaji since 2010.”
opts: I am living in Panaji from 2010.
I was living in Panaji since 2010.
I have been living in Panaji since 2010.
questions.why: 'Since' with a point in time takes the present perfect (continuous). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the part of speech of the word “beautifully”: “She sings beautifully.”
questions.why: It modifies the verb 'sings'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Find the error: “He has been living in Panaji for 2019.”
questions.why: Use 'since' with a point of time (2019); 'for' with a period (five years). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct transformation: “He is too tired to continue.”
opts: He is so tired that he cannot continue.
He is very tired that he cannot continue.
He is so tired that he can continue.
He is tired so that he cannot continue.
questions.why: 'Too ... to' becomes 'so ... that ... cannot'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “lethargic”:
questions.why: Lethargic means lacking energy. GPSC-style practice item.
